cards.anchor: Explain short returns sufficiently to choose a bounded change while targeting at least five complete twelve-counter kits and reconciliation within five minutes of placement. Five circulating complete kits and five ready shelf kits must be recorded separately; neither intervention success nor the intended availability interpretation is established.
cards.burden: Two volunteers must count, watch transfers and record demand within forty person-minutes. Only one selected tray is inspected at a time. Observation competes with checkout and may create waiting; record queue and missed events. No camera, extra counters, staff or second block is assumed.
cards.construction: Within the single twenty-minute block, verify the accounted pool and assemble five complete kits plus eleven separately accounted counters, subject to counts. Prospectively select sequential ordinary and direct-to-own-tray returns under the same predeclared demand and checkout eligibility. Retain numbered open trays and self-service shelf; instruct only the intervention borrower to put loose counters into their corresponding tray. Preserve full five-minute use and active loans. Obtain separately recorded checkout and initial return counts before sharing results. One volunteer watches placement and all subsequent selected transfers while the other counts. Record placement, borrower arrival, shortage report, search and volunteer transfer in seconds; inspect tray and mat at placement and one, three and five minutes when feasible. Withhold undocumented supplementation until observations are recorded. Log any subsequent kit repair separately from borrower-origin evidence. Never issue eleven counters. Record late placement or block-end truncation without extending the block.
cards.defeat: An agreed shortage persisting beyond five minutes, insufficient complete kits under the stated availability interpretation, excessive inspection overlap or observation requiring another block defeats demonstrated outcome preservation. A count rise explained only by volunteer supplementation defeats borrower-delayed completion for that watched recovery. No watched shortage, missing transfer coverage or count disagreement leaves causal discrimination inconclusive.
cards.mutation: Separate causal attribution from inventory repair: a loose counter can restore twelve physically without establishing completion of that borrower's return. Test the own-tray link while preserving the preferred self-service operation.
cards.prediction_candidate: Provisional H1 predicts a directly watched corresponding borrower places a final counter after tray placement and before volunteer search or transfer, followed by independently agreed twelve. In the intervention this arrival should enter its own tray. That sequence supports H1 for that loan only; historical recoveries remain unattributed.
cards.prediction_rival: H2 or shortage-triggered repair predicts unrelated traffic, search or volunteer transfer precedes the count rise. Own-tray routing may remove a communal exchange path without proving H1. H3 predicts disagreement before movement or a recount reaching twelve with no arrival; agreement can still share error. Pressure may precede both hurried counts and redistribution, but recording that association does not prove causation.
cards.probe: Compare the preselected ordinary and intervention event sequences, including the first physical transfer preceding any independently agreed eleven-to-twelve change. Hold planned demand fixed and record deviations, active loans, waiting borrowers and remaining seconds. Count-only improvement is insufficient: discriminate borrower arrival, unrelated transfer, volunteer repair and no-transfer recount. Observe one selected return through its deadline before inspecting the next; if feasible sequential coverage is unavailable, report the unmatched or truncated comparison.
cards.rival: Cross-loan redistribution, shortage-triggered volunteer repair, count error, and checkout pressure can generate apparent recovery without delayed completion by the corresponding borrower.
unknowns: Historical counter origins, unresolved counter location and initial count accuracy remain unknown.
A small block may yield no informative anomaly; attention, compliance and sequential timing may differ between conditions.
Whether five available kits means circulating complete inventory or five simultaneously ready shelf kits requires clarification; active loans prevent assuming the latter.
Independent counts may share error, and unwatched movements remain unattributed.
Keeping five kits complete after further unresolved shortages and meeting every five-minute deadline are untested.
